title: Short-staffed Sheriff: top jail overtime and an $18.0 million guard contract

beats.text: June 2025. Public Health asks to hire private guards for the City’s hospitals and clinics.

visual.text: The San Francisco Sheriff's Office has provided these services but acknowledged that they are experiencing significant staffing challenges

beats.text: Its reason: the Sheriff’s Office did the work, but faces significant staffing challenges.

visual.text: The San Francisco Sheriff's Office has provided these services but acknowledged that they are experiencing significant staffing challenges

beats.text: And the Sheriff’s overtime? 47.6 percent of regular pay.

beats.text: First of 13 sheriff and jail payrolls in California.

visual.label: Sheriff and jails overtime as a share of regular pay, 2025: first of 13

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: The first lead. In 2025, that overtime came to 58.7 million dollars.
55,706 dollars per paid position.
The middle of the others: 24,258.
In fiscal 2023-24 it overspent its whole salary budget:

beats.text: The second lead is the contract.

visual.kicker: The second lead · unarmed guards, hospitals and clinics

beats.text: Asked: 30 million dollars, 60 months. Approved: 18 million, 36.

visual.kicker: The second lead · unarmed guards, hospitals and clinics

beats.text: Yet the request is marked a temporary basis.
It wasn’t the first ask. Public Health sought private guards in 2023, and twice in 2024.

beats.text: Private guards already held hospital posts,
under City contracts since February 2023: 21.2 million dollars paid.
The third lead. The form asks: does the City have employees with the skills?

visual.title: The request form

beats.text: So when the City can’t staff its own posts, a vacancy is paid twice.

visual.line: once in overtime, once in the contract

beats.text: The fourth lead: Police overtime,

visual.label: Police overtime, share of regular pay, 2025

beats.text: 37.7 percent of regular pay in 2025. First of 7.
The fifth lead: who was told.
The notice named one class, Sheriff’s Cadet, and one union, SEIU Local 1021.
But 76.9 percent of the Sheriff’s overtime went to the deputies’ unit.

visual.label: of the Sheriff’s $62.2 million overtime, fiscal 2026

beats.text: The notice doesn’t name it.

visual.label: of the Sheriff’s $62.2 million overtime, fiscal 2026

beats.text: No reason appears in the files. Cadets aren’t sworn deputies.
Behind the overtime: the deputies’ agreement carries the jail minimums.

visual.line: The Sheriff shall reasonably determine and adjust minimum staffing for the Custody Operations Division and Court Services in Appendix B
visual.kicker: Deputy sheriffs’ agreement · 5 of 5 full texts since 2014

beats.text: Its Appendix B sets minimum deputies per shift, for each jail and court post.

visual.label: Appendix B
visual.sub: minimum supervisors and deputies per shift, each jail and court post

beats.text: In June 2019, the Controller wrote that these agreements dictate minimum staff each shift.

visual.text: These agreements dictate minimum numbers of staff the department must schedule on each shift at each jail to maintain safe and secure operations

beats.text: The records can’t tie overtime to each post.

visual.label: Overtime by post
visual.sub: cannot be tied to each Appendix B post from the records on disk

beats.text: The records don’t show any overtime went unworked, or what the guards cost against it.
